1d9b395ae6119b97b035eed0b0634607a7f0d9a3.summary: Malpedia family page for Crimson RAT, first discovered in 2017 and used against organizations around the world. The page says it is often distributed through phishing emails or by exploiting vulnerabilities in outdated security software. Once installed it can steal data, spy on users, take control of infected computers, lock them, and extort payments. The page lists many third-party reports, mostly by title, linking the malware to APT36 and Transparent Tribe activity against India. The page itself makes no attribution.

1d2a2587e69517b4af1af2aca67f3048e624583c.summary: Bitdefender white paper on a forensic investigation of a mid-2018 targeted attack on an Eastern European financial institution, attributed to the Carbanak group. Spear-phishing emails with tampered Word documents delivered Cobalt Strike beacon components. Attackers moved laterally, collected internal banking documentation and aimed at the ATM network. The timeline runs from initial compromise on Day 0 to about Day 63, largely outside business hours. The report says damage was limited to access to internal documents and leaked user credentials.

hedges: Country targeting is described as 'allegedly' targeted, not confirmed by the report.
The link between Carbanak and Cobalt Strike use is described as 'believed', not established.
The report says it 'appears' the group first mapped internal processes and applications; this is inferred from behaviour.
The financially motivated purpose is inferred ('point to a financially motivated attack').
Whether the group could have cashed out ATMs is described as 'potentially' and as a hypothetical ('If the attack had succeeded').
The claim that the group improves its tools from stolen documentation is hedged as 'could be actively improving'.
Some spear-phishing campaigns are described as 'attributed to Carbanak' by security researchers, not confirmed.
The report notes its timeline is compiled from correlated forensic evidence and that some stages are 'potentially' part of similar campaigns.
